title: A compactly supported current in ℝ^P has mass and boundary mass at most those of its restriction to an open set containing its support
statement: Assume (VO): for all P, n, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0 (the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, appearing verbatim as the first hypothesis). Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, C ⊆ U compact and Y ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with spt Y ⊆ C. Then M(Y) ≤ M(Y|_U) and M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂(Y|_U)), where Y|_U = Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U), M(Y) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y) and M(Y|_U) = M_U(Y|_U).
lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U C : Set (Euclid P)) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1)), IsOpen U → IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → Y.support ⊆ C → Y.mass ≤ (Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)).mass ∧ Y.boundary.mass ≤ (Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U)).boundary.mass
